game: Kansas State Wildcats@Arizona State Sun Devils

guide_enrichment.narrative:
Our disagreement with the market starts with Kansas State’s rushing efficiency against an Arizona State run defense that our numbers view as vulnerable. We are not treating one result as proof, but Baylor’s 244 rushing yards against Arizona State reinforce the broader concern. If Kansas State can stay efficient on the ground, it can control favorable situations and limit the pressure on its passing game.

Arizona State has enough passing production to challenge that view. Cutter Boley threw for 1,040 yards with 10 touchdowns and three interceptions through four games, while Reed Harris had 499 receiving yards and five scores. Still, our numbers favor Kansas State’s pass defense in that matchup, and Arizona State’s 29.6 percent third-down conversion rate raises questions about sustaining drives.

For us, the case for Kansas State is less about Arizona State’s recent loss and more about how these efficiency matchups fit together. We see a plausible path to separation, but the current price does not give us enough value to turn that model disagreement into a wager.
guide_enrichment.matchup_to_watch: We are watching Kansas State’s rushing offense against Arizona State’s front. Our numbers identify that as Kansas State’s cleanest advantage, and Arizona State was allowing 154.3 rushing yards per game through four games. If Kansas State consistently creates manageable downs, our more favorable expectation becomes easier to justify; if Arizona State forces obvious passing situations, the gap between our view and the market becomes less meaningful.

recent_game.fact: Arizona State fell to 2-2 overall and 1-1 in Big 12 play after a 55-19 home loss to Baylor on Oct. 3.
Arizona State gained 409 total yards, including 310 passing yards, against Baylor.
Baylor gained 564 total yards against Arizona State, including 244 rushing and 320 passing yards.
Linebacker Owen Long recorded a season-high 14 tackles against Baylor; Martell Hughes had eight tackles and two tackles for loss, and C.J. Fite had four tackles, 1.5 tackles for loss and one sack.

quarterback.fact: Kentucky transfer Cutter Boley was named Arizona State's starting quarterback before the 2026 opener.
Through four games, Boley had completed 78 of 127 passes for 1,040 yards, 10 touchdowns and three interceptions while rushing for 45 yards and one touchdown.
Boley completed 25 of 43 passes for 304 yards, one touchdown and one interception against Baylor.
Boley had thrown at least one touchdown pass in each of Arizona State's first four games.

offensive_personnel.fact: Arizona State's 2026 roster includes 30 collegiate transfers and 18 incoming freshmen, with the 48 newcomers accounting for 44.9 percent of the 107-player roster.
Wide receiver Reed Harris had 26 receptions for 499 yards and five touchdowns through four games, including three 100-yard receiving games.
Harris caught seven passes for 125 yards against Baylor, while Omarion Miller caught five passes for 85 yards and a touchdown.

Harris transferred from Boston College after recording 39 catches for 673 yards and five touchdowns in 2025, while Miller transferred from Colorado after leading that team with 45 receptions, 808 yards and eight touchdowns in 2025.

defensive_personnel.fact: Arizona State entered 2026 with four new starters in the secondary following the departures of cornerbacks Keith Abney and Javan Robinson.
Cornerbacks Rodney Bimage and Ashton Stamps had allowed completion percentages of 44.4 and 47.4 percent when targeted, respectively, through four games.
Linebacker Owen Long led Arizona State with 39 tackles through four games, 10 more than any other Sun Devil.
Martell Hughes ranked second on the team with 29 tackles and led Arizona State with 5.5 tackles for loss through four games.
Defensive lineman C.J. Fite had started 31 consecutive games and had 83 career tackles, 14.5 tackles for loss and five sacks.

coaching_changes.fact: Marcus Arroyo is Arizona State's offensive coordinator and quarterbacks coach, and Brian Ward is the defensive coordinator.
Saga Tuitele coaches the offensive line, A.J. Cooper coaches linebackers and coordinates the defensive run game, and Bryan Carrington coordinates the defensive passing game.
